description: The Mapping Challenge on AIcrowd, set up with the aid organisation Humanity & Inclusion under the title Building Missing Maps with Machine Learning, provides satellite image tiles and building annotations so that models can map buildings quickly in areas where maps are missing or out of date after disasters or conflicts. The training set has 280,741 tiles of 300 by 300 pixel RGB satellite imagery and the suggested validation set 60,317 tiles, each with building annotations in MS-COCO format; scoring used average precision and recall at an intersection over union of 0.5. Both challenge rounds are completed, with round 1 closing on 1 June 2018, and the page asks users to cite Mohanty and colleagues, Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence, 2020. Coverage: satellite image tiles; their locations are not described on the challenge page. Access: download from the challenge's datasets section after sign-up. Licence: AIcrowd challenge terms. Caveats: tiles are small and the task is binary building detection, without building attributes. Simulation uses are training footprint extraction models for humanitarian exposure mapping. Related records: the Open Cities AI Challenge dataset and SpaceNet.
